# Lumilens Emerges from Stealth with More Than $900 Million in Funding to Break AI’s Connectivity Constraint

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/69087fdd0a5d4884972a52cc/6a58e483b588832a4c8ab065_image%20306821%20(1).png)

- Founded to solve the AI connectivity constraints confronting the world's largest hyperscalers
- Now shipping into production data centers under a multi-billion-dollar customer agreement
- Developing optical interconnect technology designed to connect thousands of GPUs as a single AI system
- Raised more than $700 million in its latest financing, bringing total funding to over $900 million at a valuation of $5.51 billion

‍

SAN JOSE, Calif. — August 6, 2026 — [Lumilens](https://lumilens.com/), the connectivity platform for AI infrastructure, today emerged from stealth, having been founded to solve the growing networking bottlenecks limiting AI scale. In just two years after its founding, the company is commercially shipping its first product into production AI data centers under a multi-billion-dollar customer agreement, and announced more than $700 million in new funding co-led by [Atreides Management](https://atreidesmgmt.com/), [Bain Capital Ventures](https://baincapitalventures.com/), [Meritech](https://www.meritechcapital.com/), [Seligman Ventures](https://www.seligman.com/) and [Spark Capital](https://www.sparkcapital.com/), with participation from [Addition](https://www.addition.com/), [AICONIC VENTURES](https://aiconicventures.com/), [Alkeon](https://www.alkeoncapital.com/), [Harbourvest](https://www.harbourvest.com/us/en), [J.P. Morgan Private Capital](https://am.jpmorgan.com/us/en/asset-management/mod/growth-equity-partners/), [Mayfield](https://www.mayfield.com/), [MVP Ventures](https://mvp-vc.com/), [Qualcomm Ventures](https://www.qualcommventures.com/), [Peak XV,](https://peakxv.com/) [Redpoint Ventures](https://www.redpoint.com/), [Seifdune](https://seifdune.com/) and other top-tier investors. The financing values the company at $5.51 billion and brings its total capital raised to over $900 million.

The world's largest technology companies are spending historic sums on AI infrastructure — Citigroup projects the total will cross [$2.8 trillion by 2029](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/citigroup-forecasts-big-techs-ai-spending-cross-28-trillion-by-2029-2025-09-30/) — but buying GPUs is no longer the hard part. Connecting them is. Modern AI models are trained and served across hundreds of thousands of processors that must behave as a single computer, and the performance of that computer is now determined as much by the network linking those chips as by the chips themselves.

The challenge is emerging in two critical places inside the AI data center: scale-out and scale-up fabrics.

In the scale-out fabric that ties racks and rows of GPUs together, every processor added multiplies the optical transceivers required. A single 400,000 GPU data center requires more than 2.4 million transceivers and more than five million fiber strands from a market already unable to keep pace. [McKinsey projects](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/technology-media-and-telecommunications/our-insights/opportunities-in-networking-optics-boosting-supply-for-data-centers) that 800G optical transceiver production could fall 40–60% short of industry demand through 2027, with 1.6T transceiver shortfalls of 30–40% persisting through 2029.

Inside the rack, physics has imposed a ceiling on the scale-up fabric, where GPUs are wired directly to one another over copper connections. At the data rates AI demands, electrical signals survive only about a meter and a half over copper, confining a tightly coupled domain to a single rack and hundreds of GPUs. When a hyperscaler roadmap calls for thousands of GPUs, breaking that ceiling means replacing copper with photonics.

Lumilens was born to address that constraint. In early 2024, the founding team set out to solve the connectivity problems the largest AI clusters foreshadowed — problems a top hyperscaler was already confronting as it sized the clusters its AI roadmap would require. In just two years later, Lumilens' initial scale-out product finished qualification and started shipping into that hyperscaler's production AI data centers under a multi-billion-dollar agreement. Lumilens designs and manufactures optical interconnects for both types of networks inside an AI data center — the scale-up network that directly connects GPUs together within a single compute system, and the scale-out fabric that stitches different racks and clusters together.

> "The constraint on AI has shifted from how many GPUs you can buy to how many you can connect," said [Ankur Singla](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ankur-singla-4863801/), founder and CEO of Lumilens. "Whether they're training frontier models or serving them to hundreds of millions of users, hyperscalers told us they need the same two things: far more optical capacity for the networks they run today, and a path to directly connecting thousands of GPUs together into a single cluster. We built Lumilens to deliver both — and to manufacture at the volume, quality, and pace this buildout demands."
>
> ‍ _Ankur Singla_ **_CEO & founder of lumilens_**

The Lumilens portfolio spans the full connectivity stack of an AI data center:

- **Scale-up silicon and systems (NPO and CPO) —** near-package and co-packaged optics that bring optical I/O directly to the GPU, enabling thousands of processors — and, on the company’s roadmap, tens of thousands — to operate as a single, tightly coupled domain
- **Scale-out pluggable transceivers (800G, 1.6T, and beyond) —** optical modules that replace copper links across racks and rows, carrying more data at lower power for the largest AI fabrics

Every product is built on LumiCore™, the company’s unified technology platform spanning silicon photonics, mixed-signal ICs, electrical-optical interposers, and optical systems, all developed in-house. A single platform across the portfolio lets Lumilens move from design to customer-qualified product in months rather than years, and ensures each product is engineered for high-volume manufacturing from day one.

At Lumilens, manufacturing is treated as a product in its own right. The company has designed a ground-breaking electrical-optical interposer technology that dramatically simplifies photonic chip assembly, along with proprietary manufacturing process recipes, custom robotics, and test automation — scaling capacity through manufacturing partners and its own large-scale facilities. The model gives customers something the optics industry has rarely offered: rapid innovation in performance and density, matched by the ability to scale production just as quickly.

> "Over the past several years, the conversation around AI infrastructure has centered on access to compute," said [Umesh Padval](https://www.linkedin.com/in/umesh-padval-7a06b85/), Managing Partner, Seligman Ventures. "Increasingly, the constraint today is shifting to connectivity and how efficiently thousands of GPUs can operate as a single system. We are excited to partner with Ankur Singla, a proven repeat founder who has assembled a world-class team spanning silicon, optics, software, systems, supply chain and manufacturing expertise to address one of the most important challenges in modern data centers. Lumilens' early hyperscaler adoption and multi-billions in customer commitments just two years after its founding reflects both the scale of the opportunity and the team's ability to execute.."
>
> _Umesh Padval_ **_Managing Partner, Seligman Ventures_**

> "The critical component in scaling AI is shifting from compute to connectivity," said [Gavin Baker](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gavinbaker-portfoliomanager/), Managing Partner at Atreides Management. “Focusing on that core AI challenge, Lumilens went from its founding to a qualified product deployed inside a hyperscaler's production data centers within two years, and is building the manufacturing engine to scale with demand while bringing much-needed diversification to AI supply chains. Speed and scale are a formidable combination, and we're thrilled to lead this round."
>
> _Gavin Baker_ **_Managing Partner, Atreides Management_**

> "Connecting GPUs is the bottleneck now, and copper has hit a wall the industry can't engineer around," said [Navin Chaddha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/navinchaddha/), Managing Partner at Mayfield. "That's why we partnered with Ankur Singla for the third time to help build Lumilens from inception, led their seed round, and have participated in every round since. Lumilens designs and manufactures optical interconnects for both the scale-up and scale-out of AI infrastructure, and treats manufacturing as a product in its own right, from chip assembly to high-volume production. In Mayfield’s 56-year history, we've never seen execution and growth like this – a $5+ billion valuation and multi-billions in orders – in two years"
>
> _Navin Chaddha_ **_Managing Partner, Mayfield_**

> "Lumilens is addressing critical connectivity challenges for scaling AI by delivering best-in-class solutions for both scale-out and scale-up networks," said James Kuklinski, General Partner at Spark Capital. "We're proud to partner with Ankur Singla and the world-class team at Lumilens — a rare combination of deep expertise in silicon photonics, networking systems and high-volume manufacturing — as they are uniquely positioned to build a defining company in this generational AI infrastructure buildout. We first partnered with Lumilens by leading the Series B in early 2025 and are thrilled to have doubled down to co-lead the Series C financing, given the team's rapid execution, vast ambition, and the scale of the market opportunity ahead."
>
> _James Kuklinski_ **_General Partner at Spark Capital_**

‍

To execute on the $100+ billion market opportunity for photonic interconnects2, Lumilens has assembled a leadership team with deep expertise in both photonics and large-scale networking systems, including executives and engineers from Cisco, Juniper Networks, Meta, Marvell, Lumentum, and Coherent.

The Lumilens Series C funding round includes participation from a wide range of top-tier investors: Addition, AICONIC VENTURES, Alkeon, Atreides Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, EDBI (arm of SG Growth Capital, the investment platform of EDB and Enterprise Singapore), Harbourvest, J.P. Morgan Private Capital, Lingotto, Mayfield, Meritech, MVP Ventures, Peak XV, Qualcomm Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Seifdune, Seligman Ventures, Spark Capital and Thomvest Ventures. The new funding will help the Company expand its rapidly growing silicon, systems, software, process engineering, and high-volume manufacturing operations.

#### About Lumilens

Lumilens is the connectivity platform for AI infrastructure, delivering scale-up and scale-out optical interconnect solutions designed for the performance, power, and bandwidth demands of next-generation AI workloads. The company designs, develops, and manufactures near-package optics (NPO), co-packaged optics (CPO), and pluggable optical transceivers for hyperscaler AI data centers. Built on Lumilens' own silicon photonics, mixed-signal ICs, electrical-optical interposers, and optical systems, the LumiCore platform enables tighter integration, higher bandwidth density, lower power consumption, and greater flexibility across AI network architectures. Lumilens is backed by Addition, Atreides Management, Bain Capital Ventures, Mayfield, Meritech, Redpoint Ventures, Seligman Ventures, Spark Capital, and other leading venture capital and private investors. For more information, visit [Lumilens.com](https://lumilens.com/).
